candidate.title: GRO-Seq/BRIC-Seq/Bru-Seq/BruChase-Seq
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina GRO-Seq/BRIC-Seq/Bru-Seq/BruChase-Seq grouped card, at schematic and member-interface scope. Five operations preserve the single drawn route: Br-UTP run-on on nascent RNA, isolation/hydrolysis, antibody-bead capture, grouped elution/cap removal/end repair, and RT/amplification to cDNA. That material history is primary-supported for GRO-Seq. The other three card targets are retained as distinct assays: separate literature-supported capture-to-library local interfaces resolve their applicability without assigning them the run-on-derived input states. These six interface operations are explicitly not additional branches depicted in the PNG; cellular labeling/chase occurs only in their supported boundary histories. Candidate collection pages 30, 32 and 33 were checked by heading and target: page 30 corroborates GRO-Seq; pages 32/33 clarify their own named members at catalogue evidence level, not the arrows in the assigned image. No complete cellular-labeling workflow, time-series graph, pooling, adapter sequence, sequencing operation, implementation equivalence or historical lineage is reconstructed.

evidence.quote: GRO-Seq maps the binding sites of transcriptionally active RNA polymerase II (RNAPII). In this method, active RNAPII is allowed to run on in the presence of 5-bromouridine 5'-triphosphate (Br-UTP). RNAs are hydrolyzed and purified using beads coated with antibodies to 5-bromo-2-deoxyuridine (BrdU). After cap removal and end repair, the eluted RNA is reverse-transcribed to cDNA. Deep sequencing of the cDNA identifies RNAs that are actively transcribed by RNAPII.

evidence.locator: jcr:content/par/text_0/text: GRO-Seq description
evidence.quote: GRO-Seq maps the binding sites of transcriptionally active RNA polymerase II (RNAPII). In this method, active RNAPII is allowed to run on in the presence of 5-bromouridine 5'-triphosphate (Br-UTP). RNAs are hydrolyzed and purified using beads coated with antibodies to 5-bromo-2-deoxyuridine (BrdU). After cap removal and end repair, the eluted RNA is reverse-transcribed to cDNA. Deep sequencing of the cDNA identifies RNAs that are actively transcribed by RNAPII.
